title: First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future Together Gathers ASEAN First Spouses For Event Hosted by Philippine First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Media Note


			
			


			
			
November 19, 2026
On November 16, First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future Together initiative brought leaders together in Manila for an event focused on child online protection, hosted by Philippine First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos. The event advanced Mrs. Trump’s global leadership to empower children and keep them safe in the digital age.
Mrs. Araneta-Marcos co-hosted the event with the Philippines Child Protection Network. She welcomed visiting ASEAN First Spouses and about 150 leaders from government, civil society, and the private sector, including leading U.S. tech companies, such as Google, Intel, Meta, and Microsoft. A panel of child protection experts and a speaker from Intel shared practical ways to keep children safe online.
U.S. Ambassador Lee Lipton spoke about the strong partnership between the United States and the Philippines to protect children. He pointed to the U.S. Embassy’s close work with Philippine law enforcement, prosecutors, and advocates to fight online crimes against children. He praised Mrs. Trump for turning partnership into action. Ambassador Lipton noted that in just one year she has united nearly 60 First Spouses and equivalent leaders so that no child is held back by geography or circumstance. He added that Mrs. Trump understands children deserve every opportunity to succeed and that their safety must always come first.
Mrs. Araneta-Marcos joined Fostering the Future Together in September, and this gathering reflects her commitment to children in the Philippines and throughout Southeast Asia. The United States applauds her leadership.
Through Fostering the Future Together, Mrs. Trump and her coalition partners are opening doors to education and technology, keeping children safe online, and preparing young people for the age of Super Intelligence (SI). First Lady Melania Trump’s message to the gathering may be viewed here.

title: Targeting Cyber Scam Center Enablers in Southeast Asia
summary_raw:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
Press Statement


			
			


			
			
November 19, 2026
Today, the United States is sanctioning five individuals and entities that own, operate, and enable cyber scam centers in Cambodia and Burma. These criminal enterprises steal billions of dollars from victims around the world, including Americans. The Department of the Treasury designated Zhao Hui, who operated a scam center in Cambodia, and two Cambodia-based companies he controls. Treasury also designated two senior leaders of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA): commander-in-chief General Saw Shwe Wah, and Colonel Saw A One, who oversees security and participate in violence against victims of human trafficking trapped inside the scam centers.
This action supports President Trump’s Executive Order 14390, “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” which directs the U.S. government to use every available tool against foreign-backed criminal networks that prey on Americans through cybercrime, cyber-enabled fraud, and extortion. Southeast Asia–based scam centers, most of them run by Chinese organized crime groups, stole an estimated $18.2 billion from Americans in 2025. These scam centers fuel human trafficking, enrich armed groups, and undermine the rule of law and stability in Southeast Asia.
The Department of the Treasury took this action in coordination with the Department of Justice’s Scam Center Strike Force, the Homeland Security Task Force and National Coordination Center, the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s New York Field Office, and the Drug Enforcement Administration.
The United States calls on governments in the region to shut down scam operations, prosecute their leaders, owners, and protectors, and identify and assist trafficking victims. The United States will keep working with partners in Southeast Asia and around the world to dismantle these networks, hold accountable those who enable them, and protect Americans from fraud.
OFAC is taking today’s actions pursuant to E.O. 13694, as amended. For more information, see Treasury’s press release.

title: Sanctioning Major International Drug Trafficking Organizations Linked to Foreign Terrorist Organizations
summary_raw:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
Press Statement


			
			


			
			
November 19, 2026

Today, the United States is sanctioning two international drug trafficking organizations (DTOs): the Australia-headquartered Comanchero Outlaw Motorcycle Gang (Comancheros) and the Italy-based ‘Ndrangheta. Both groups provide essential logistical support to designated Foreign Terrorist Organizations (FTOs), including the Sinaloa Cartel, Cártel de Jalisco Nueva Generación, and Clan del Golfo. These sanctions are being implemented by the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC).
The Comancheros and ‘Ndrangheta play a critical role in perpetuating the global illicit drug trade. They move drug shipments, launder money, and carry out other criminal operations, enabling FTOs to extend their criminal operations across international borders and sustain global narcotics trafficking networks. These sanctions will disrupt the financial infrastructure of these DTOs, which will cut off critical support to the cartels that flood our communities with deadly drugs and help protect American lives.
The United States will pursue anyone who does business with FTOs, as well as their associated assets and criminal enterprises, wherever they try to hide. No one who finances or profits from cartel violence and destruction will find safe haven.
Today’s action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14059, which targets the proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production.
For more information about today’s sanctions, please see the Department of the Treasury’s press release.
